transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in today?

Hello Dr. Lee, I'm Tracey. I'm here because I’m constantly forgetting little everyday things—appointments, errands, even finishing what I start for the community center. My husband and friends were actually worried I was developing early dementia, but my primary care doctor suggested it might be a long-standing attention issue instead.
When did these difficulties with attention and forgetfulness first start? Were they present during your childhood or did they become noticeable more recently?

They've become much more noticeable and disruptive over the last two years since I retired, but these issues actually go all the way back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, my report cards always said I daydreamed, rushed, and talked out of turn, and my mother would scold me for wandering off halfway through my chores. It seems I've always struggled with this, but I used to have more structure to keep me on track.

F32.9 (unspecified depressive episode) is also less likely because the patient attributes her symptoms to attention and executive functioning issues rather than mood disturbance, and the lifelong history points away from a primary mood disorder as the root cause. The persistent nature of attentional difficulties since childhood strongly supports F90.0 (hyperkinetic disorder, i.e., ADHD) as the most consistent diagnosis.
